name: Texas Is the Reason
label: Revelation
lede: Nine songs, one album, a name taken from a line in the Misfits song "Bullet", and a band that broke up in Germany on the eve of a Capitol deal, which is how the record became Revelation's best seller instead of a major-label debut.

eras.title: Krishnacore kids go melodic
eras.text: Texas Is the Reason's two founders came out of the most devout corner of hardcore: Norman Brannon had played guitar in Shelter as Norman Arenas, and Chris Daly had drummed in 108. With Copper singer Garrett Klahn and bassist Scott Winegard, they made something warmer and more open-ended, and New York clubs started booking them as the opener everybody showed up early for.

years.cap: Texas Is the Reason · via Discogs
years.h: Named after a line in the Misfits song "Bullet"
years.p: Norman Brannon and Chris Daly add bassist [[Scott Winegard|400a7302-6a36-4c80-b5fc-17d3d0d4e3cf]] and singer-guitarist [[Garrett Klahn|f6190334-6d61-473a-9992-c4791da7adc6]]. [[Chris Leo|df1ce5f2-cfb5-4c81-84b6-4a4e9a6a5927]] of [[The Van Pelt|4ce909db-0da6-4eed-bfe6-6c1f71e265b0]] suggests the name Texas Is the Reason, taken from the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] song "Bullet" about the JFK assassination.
years.xp:
Revelation's bio traces the members back through Shelter, 108 and Resurrection, a family tree of early-'90s hardcore that sounds nothing like the band they became.

Brannon was still Norman Arenas then, and edited the zine Anti-Matter. He changed his surname legally in 2004, and has written that almost everyone mispronounced Arenas.

years.h: Debut EP Texas Is the Reason on Revelation
years.p: The self-titled 1995 EP on Revelation Records moves Texas Is the Reason from opening slots to headlining New York shows almost immediately.
Texas Is the Reason share a 7-inch with the band Samuel, released by Simba Recordings and Art Monk Construction, the kind of small-run record that got passed around at shows.

eras.title: Do you know who you are?
eras.text: Texas Is the Reason made one full-length, Do You Know Who You Are?: nine songs, under forty minutes. The title is the question John Lennon was reportedly asked just before he was shot. Garrett Klahn was 21, and major labels were already calling.

years.h: Do You Know Who You Are?, recorded with J. Robbins, on Revelation
years.p: Cut at Oz Studios in Baltimore in December 1995 with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] co-producing, Texas Is the Reason's only album becomes Revelation's best-selling release.
years.xp:
Drew Mazurek engineered the Oz Studios sessions, and the songs were already road-tested. Vlad Meller mastered the record at Sony Music Studios, and Glenn Maryansky designed the sleeve.

Do You Know Who You Are? made best-of lists from Rolling Stone, LA Weekly and NME, and Spin, Alternative Press and Paste later put it among the essential records of the '90s. Critics kept coming back to Garrett Klahn's voice, warm without taking over. It was the only album Texas Is the Reason ever made.
play: Do You Know Who You Are?

years.h: Split EP with [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]] on Jade Tree
years.p: Texas Is the Reason and The Promise Ring, two of the bands that would define '90s emo, share one record on Jade Tree.

years.h: Major labels chase Texas Is the Reason. Capitol wins
years.p: Through a year of heavy touring behind Do You Know Who You Are?, major labels court Texas Is the Reason, and the band agrees to sign with Capitol Records.

eras.title: Eight hundred Germans and a way out
eras.text: About ten months after Do You Know Who You Are? came out, Texas Is the Reason stopped. It happened on a 1997 European tour, with a Capitol deal waiting at home, and the members have told it as a clean decision rather than a blowup.

q: There were eight hundred Germans singing along with us.
years.h: Texas Is the Reason's last show: Bielefeld, Germany
years.p: The final show of the 1997 European tour is in Bielefeld. Norman Brannon remembers the crowd singing every word, looking over at Chris Daly, and knowing the band was done.
years.xp:
Garrett Klahn's version, told to Paste: the band had agreed that if the Bielefeld show was great, they'd end Texas Is the Reason there. The split came at Frankfurt airport, with the Capitol deal set for the next day in his telling.

Wikipedia has them touring Europe before signing with Capitol. Either way, there was no major-label album. Daly went on to [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]] with [[Blake Schwarzenbach|c7d68007-b688-426f-a496-08467a0a6f44]]; Klahn formed New Rising Sons.

eras.title: Anniversaries only
eras.text: Texas Is the Reason reunited on round-number anniversaries of Do You Know Who You Are?, and the New York shows sold out fast. Each run was pitched as a last time, and each time the band came back.

years.cap: Texas Is the Reason · via Discogs
years.h: First reunion: two sold-out nights at Irving Plaza
years.p: Texas Is the Reason reunite in New York for the tenth anniversary of Do You Know Who You Are?, selling out two nights at Irving Plaza.

years.h: Reunion shows at Irving Plaza and Music Hall of Williamsburg
years.p: Texas Is the Reason play another New York run, sixteen years after Do You Know Who You Are?.
Revelation remasters all of Texas Is the Reason's recordings and adds two previously unreleased songs. A limited North American tour follows.

years.h: A "final" reunion show at the Electric Ballroom, London
years.p: Texas Is the Reason bill their London show at the Electric Ballroom as their last one.

years.h: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, February 16, 2013
yt: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, February 16, 2013

years.h: Twenty years on: Saint Vitus, Brooklyn
years.p: Texas Is the Reason sell out the small Brooklyn metal bar Saint Vitus for the twentieth anniversary of Do You Know Who You Are?. A second night gets added.

years.h: A benefit show for singer Jon Bunch in Philadelphia
years.p: At the TLA in Philadelphia, Texas Is the Reason play a benefit for the late [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]] and [[Further Seems Forever|2bc3d11f-58fe-4adb-bfd9-6d316973005a]] singer Jon Bunch, raising money for his son's college fund.
years.xp: [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] and a reunited Sense Field were also on the bill.

eras.title: Nine months in a room
eras.text: For the 2025 return, Texas Is the Reason rehearsed for most of a year before telling anyone, then toured further than it ever had in the '90s. It went without founder Norman Brannon, who explained why on his own terms.

years.h: Texas Is the Reason rehearse in secret
years.p: Garrett Klahn says the band spent nine or ten months in a room getting the fourteen songs of its set right, without telling anybody.

years.h: Norman Brannon sits out the reunion
years.p: Norman Brannon says revisiting Texas Is the Reason means revisiting his mid-'90s life as a closeted gay man, and he doesn't want to. John Herguth plays guitar in his place.
years.xp: Brannon added that there's no bad blood with the band.

years.cap: Texas Is the Reason · via Discogs
years.h: Texas Is the Reason play Best Friends Forever, Las Vegas
years.p: The reunited band plays the festival at the Downtown Las Vegas Events Center, October 10–12, on a bill with reunions from [[Rilo Kiley|eaf6a7ca-105d-4a94-ba02-8c3e4040319a]] and [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]].

years.h: Texas Is the Reason tour Australia and Japan for the first time
years.p: The 2026 run takes Texas Is the Reason to Australia and Japan for the first time, to Primavera Sound, and onto dates with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]] and [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]]. Garrett Klahn says no new songs are planned unless they come naturally.
